subject: MCP Health: hosting posture, GPU slate & procurement alignment
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@mcph.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: MCP pilot — hosting posture & GPU slate (quick alignment)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time last week. Before we build the pilot SOW, want to align on two things that materially affect cost and procurement timelines:

1) Hosting posture: are you comfortable with Redwood Dedicated (reserved private pools in our cloud tenancy) or do you need a Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem) deployment for the pilot? From our side the main differences for pilot sizing are:
   - Dedicated: faster start (2–4 weeks), we provision reserved GPU nodes in our tenancy; supports SOC2 + VLAN isolation; limited air-gap options.
   - Private: longer lead time (6–10+ weeks), supports customer VPC or on‑prem with HSM/KMS integration and stricter network isolation.

2) Target model & QPS expectations: knowing the model (LlamaX-70B quantized vs. LlamaX-13B) and expected peak QPS will determine the GPU slate. If you can share an expected 95th percentile tokens/sec or peak daily requests we can propose a concrete slate.

Attached a short one‑pager that compares the high‑level tradeoffs and a preliminary workbook for GPU slate estimates. Quick asks: can you confirm (A) hosting posture preference for the pilot, (B) whether procurement needs an air‑gapped/physical isolation option, and (C) preliminary QPS or example traffic (e.g., 100 peak simultaneous sessions)?

If easier, we can join procurement/security next week — happy to coordinate.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@mcph.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security@mcph.com
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MCP pilot — hosting posture & GPU slate (quick alignment)

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from MCP Security & Procurement:

- For the pilot we are leaning toward Dedicated only if we can demonstrate network isolation + customer-specific audit logs. If we cannot reasonably guarantee air‑gap capabilities during the pilot, Procurement will push for Private (VPC with customer-managed subnets) — it's a hard requirement for the pilot legal team to avoid shared tenant compute until we complete our audit.

- Models: initially LlamaX-13B quantized for NLU/chat features, with a possible upgrade to 70B for higher-fidelity summarization in Q2.

- Traffic: rough estimate — 80 RPS peak (concurrent chat sessions ~40), average session length ~120 tokens per request, expected burstiness during morning windows.

- Procurement lead time: 45–75 days typical on our side for new contracts + any on‑prem hardware approvals.

Can you send a short note that contrasts the Dedicated configuration we would need to meet the audit (audit log retention, dedicated logging endpoints, encryption-at-rest with customer KMS, and a physical isolation option for later phases) vs. Private — and hit the timeline/cost delta? That will help our procurement team decide whether to accept a Dedicated pilot with strict SLAs or insist on Private from day one.

Thanks,
Alice
Director, Cloud Security — MCP Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@mcph.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MCP pilot — hosting posture & GPU slate (quick alignment)

Alice —

Appreciate the context — helpful. Quick contrast below to share with Procurement/Security (also attached as the one‑pager):

Dedicated (fastest pilot start)
- Timeline: 2–4 weeks to provision reserved GPUs in Redwood tenancy and enable dedicated pools for MCP only.
- Isolation: single-tenant GPU pools, logical tenancy separation; supports streaming audit logs to your SIEM, per-token tracing retention configurable up to contractual limits.
- KMS: we can integrate your KMS for encryption-at-rest via API-backed keys; HSM options are limited in hosted Dedicated but we can support customer-managed keys for disk encryption.
- Air‑gap: not full physical air‑gap; we can implement strict egress controls, private peering, and an isolated subnet, but hardware remains under Redwood operations.
- Cost: ~25–35% lower capex/OPEX for pilot compared with Private due to shared infrastructure and faster ramp.

Private (VPC / on‑prem)
- Timeline: 6–10+ weeks (longer if on‑prem provisioning required).
- Isolation: full network isolation, supports air‑gap / on‑prem; dedicated control plane optional under customer network.
- KMS/HSM: full support for customer-managed HSM/KMS, bring-your-own-hardware options for highest compliance bar.
- Cost: higher due to provisioning, networking, and dedicated hardware ops. Better for long‑term regulated production.

Preliminary GPU slate suggestion (based on LlamaX-13B quantized + 80 RPS bursts):
- Baseline pilot: 3 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) nodes in a dedicated pool, configured for continuous batching + KV cache. Adds ~30% headroom for burst.
- If you expect to upgrade to 70B in Q2: plan additional 4 nodes (A100-80GB equiv) or equivalent MCM/8-bit path for cost efficiency.

Procurement implications: if Procurement insists on Private for pilot, expect added procurement lead time (45–90 days) and an initial higher one-time provisioning fee. Dedicated lets us get data and audit logs flowing sooner but may require a contractual SLA addendum about audit log retention and encryption key handling.

Next steps suggestions:
- If Procurement can accept Dedicated with an audit-focused SLA addendum (we'll provide per-request logs + SIEM endpoint and KMS integration), we can spin a pilot in ~3 weeks.
- Otherwise, begin Private onboarding in parallel — we can start control plane prep immediately and concurrent procurement for physical/network resources.

I'll draft a short exec note for Procurement that spells out the SLA addendum we propose. Marissa/Karthik — keeping you in loop for sizing/price guidance.

Best,
Soojin

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: MCP pilot posture recommendation & next asks

Marissa / Karthik —

Quick internal summary after Alice's reply:

- MCP will likely push for Private unless we can produce a tight audit/SIEM/KMS guarantee for Dedicated. Procurement lead time on their end is non-trivial (45–75 days).
- Traffic profile: target LlamaX-13B quantized, 80 RPS peak with bursts; upgrade to 70B is probable in Q2.

My recommendation for deal engineering & pricing:
1) Offer a two-track pilot proposal: Dedicated (fast ramp) with SLA addendum vs Private (longer ramp) with a one-time provisioning fee. Price the Dedicated pilot at a premium to account for the audit guarantees — add 15% to baseline reserved price and include a refundable compliance deposit to cover special logging/retention work.
2) GPU slate: propose 3 x A100-80GB equivalent for immediate pilot (continuous batching + KV cache) + optional optional upgrade clause to add 4 nodes for 70B transition. Provide clear escape clauses for burst capacity.
3) Procurement artifact: I will draft a 1‑page SLA addendum that includes: audit log retention policies, SIEM ingestion endpoint, KMS integration notes, and acceptance criteria for isolation. We should run the addendum by Security for signoff.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you sketch a pricing line with the +15% audit addendum premium and refundable deposit?
- Karthik: please validate the 3-node slate and add a fallback reserved-hour estimate and burst cushion pricing.
- I'll draft the SLA addendum and set a joint call with MCP procurement/security for next Thu.

Thanks —
Soojin
